component.name: Lookout
component.summary: A native mail client for GNOME

description.p: Lookout is a native GNOME/libadwaita mail client. It connects to your mail accounts through GNOME Online Accounts, so there is no separate sign-in - add an account in Settings and Lookout picks it up automatically.

Added a "Background wallpaper" switch to Settings → Appearance: turning it off hides the window's wallpaper entirely and disables the background image picker, dimming slider, and restore-default options, which only matter when a wallpaper is shown.

Fixed two rough edges on desktops without GNOME Online Accounts or a GNOME-flavoured keyring, such as KDE Plasma: a spurious "Couldn't reach GNOME Online Accounts" toast and a permanently-empty accounts section in Settings no longer appear when the service simply isn't installed, and the keyring-unavailable error message no longer assumes GNOME Keyring is the only fix.
Fixed a crash when editing the Assistant settings' API key field: typing a key, pausing, then typing again could abort the app instead of just saving the change.

The Lookout tab's assistant card, renamed from "AI Chat" to "Ask" (its button now reads "Ask" too), now breaks a multi-topic reply into separate visual cards instead of one long scroll of text - each heading in the answer becomes its own card. Links in a reply are now a high-contrast blue instead of the hard-to-read default.

The Lookout tab's AI Chat card no longer shows "Asking the assistant…" text while waiting for an answer - it now shows a gently pulsing version of its idle-state robot icon instead, and a failed request shows the same icon recolored red with the error message underneath.

The Lookout tab's AI Chat card can now link straight to the emails and calendar events it mentions: replies include clickable links that jump to the exact message (switching to Mail, opening its folder, and selecting the row - expanding a collapsed section or conversation if needed) or open the exact calendar event's editor, the same way clicking a desktop notification already does. A new "upcoming events" tool lets the assistant look up real calendar events, not just tasks. Also fixes two bugs introduced while building this: chat replies briefly stopped rendering at all, and a link some models wrap in angle brackets failed to open.

The AI Chat card's empty-state robot glyph now loads through the app's standard asset pipeline - a bundled SVG resource (ai-1.svg) with the usual embedded fallback - instead of being embedded in code, so the artwork is editable as a file.

The Lookout dashboard's AI Chat card talks to the configured assistant with real data: it answers from the app's own emails, contacts, and tasks through five function-calling tools (recent mail, full-text search, most-contacted people, address-book contacts, and tasks from every source), and renders its replies as formatted HTML - markdown headings, bold, lists, code, links, tables, and embedded graphics like inline SVG - in a read-only, script-free WebView with a transparent background over the dashboard. The layout shifts too: outstanding tasks move to the right column, People most contacted shows five rows instead of eight, and the AI Chat card fills its column's full height.

Settings gains an Assistant section for configuring an OpenAI-compatible API: an API URL field (persisted in GSettings), an API token field stored in the GNOME keyring, a Test connection button that probes the server's /models endpoint and reports whether the URL and token work, and an Agent dropdown listing the API's available models with a refresh button. Dev builds also no longer crash when a stale packaged schema shadows the freshly-compiled one.

Opening email is now instant: new messages are cached the moment they arrive - their bodies download as part of the sync itself, not whenever the background prefetch gets to them - and opening a message reads the local cache directly, so already-cached mail renders without waiting on the mail session. User actions also preempt background work: message, image, and attachment fetches get their own priority lane, server-side searches yield to clicks, and the background body prefetch fetches conservatively, so nothing you're doing waits behind bulk downloads.

Signatures: a global signature library managed from Settings → Accounts (a rich-text editor creates them, Edit/Delete manage the list), per-account default signatures for new messages and replies & forwards, and a composer signature button that inserts any signature at the cursor and auto-appends each account's default when composing. Embedded signature images are stored inline, and reopening the Settings modal no longer shows it empty.

Packaging polish: the .deb now ships a DEP-5 copyright file with the full GPL-3 license text, and the appstream metainfo gains bug tracker and repository links, carousel tile branding colours, and a clean validation.

While composing in the reading pane, the rich text controls (attach, plain/rich toggle, and the formatting buttons) now live in the action bar below the menu bar, replacing the message-list buttons for the session; popping the composer out into its own window moves them back into the editor and restores the action bar. The formatting icons are built and styled exactly like the ribbon bar's default icons.

The Settings gear moved from the bottom of the left rail into the header bar, next to the window controls, and the Settings screen now opens as a modal dialog over the main window - same design as before, just no longer a side view.
In the Mail screen's "Upcoming events" section, all-day events now show the day they fall on ("Today", "Tomorrow", "Sat 5 Sep") instead of a bare "All Day".

The Mail screen's mini-calendar panel now shows an "Upcoming events" section between the selected day's events and the outstanding tasks - up to 10 events from your checked calendars over the next 90 days, fetched live as you open the Mail screen.

An empty message list (a folder with no messages) now shows a friendly placeholder - a white bird with "Folder is empty" and a quiet "The stars were bright, Fernando." - instead of a blank pane, and the loading spinner no longer lingers over an already-painted cached list.

Settings → Advanced gains an "Aggressive prefetch" mode for the background body downloader: batches run on a timer you set, more of each folder is warmed, and folders re-scan periodically - all optional, with the cooperative default unchanged while the switch is off.

An optional tray icon shows the total unread email count in the notification area - click it to show or hide the window, right-click for Open / Compose / Quit - controlled by the new "Tray icon" switch in Settings.

The app icon in the dock now shows a badge with the total unread email count - the same number as the "All Inboxes" folder - with a Config → Mail toggle to hide it. Works on Ubuntu's dock and other launchers that speak the Unity LauncherEntry protocol.

Pinning a message on a Microsoft 365 account now also pins it in Outlook itself, via an opt-in "Sync pins with Outlook" button in Settings - Lookout's own pinning still works exactly as before either way.

The "Vertical spacing" setting now spaces every entry in the folder list, not just the account headers - tight, medium, and loose all apply evenly to every row, and loose gives folders 20% more room than the message list.
The sender avatar in the message list now shows just the first letter for single-word names, and the initials of the first and last words for multi-word names.

The reading pane no longer displays remote images from senders you haven't trusted, or when "Load images from the web" is off - the block is now enforced with a Content-Security-Policy in the message itself, which WebKit honors on every load.

The "Trusted senders" dialog under Settings → Mail no longer opens empty - it now lists each connected account with its saved trusted senders and add rows, and adding or removing an entry updates the list in place.
"Star/Unstar" is now "Pin/Unpin" throughout, matching Outlook - including a new pin icon in place of the star, while the separate mailbox/contact Favorites star is unchanged.
Starred messages now pin to their own "Starred" section at the top of the message list, no matter how you're sorting - and starring or unstarring moves a message into or out of it instantly.
The message list's hover menu trades its Archive button for three toggles - Mark Read/Unread, Follow-up, and Star/Unstar - so you can update a message's state without opening it.
Settings is tidier - the "Layout" page is merged into "Appearance", so the vertical-spacing choice sits with the rest of the look-and-feel settings.
You can now choose the spacing between items in the folder and message lists - tight, medium (the default), or loose - from Settings under Appearance.
Deleting a message no longer flickers - the row could briefly reappear before being removed for good if it happened to coincide with a background sync.

The dashboard's "most contacted" and "emails by time of day" panels are now read in the background instead of on the main thread - opening it no longer pauses the interface, even for accounts with hundreds of thousands of cached messages.
Adding or reconnecting a mail account no longer pauses the interface while its local cache is set up - that work now happens in the background.
Settings is simpler - the separate "Accounts" and "Mail accounts" panels are now one "Accounts" panel, so there's a single place to add, edit, and manage your accounts.
Snippets under new mail arrive faster and cheaper - fetching a message preview no longer re-reads and re-sends the entire folder's list, just the handful of messages that actually got a snippet.

Faster mail syncing for large folders - fixed an inefficiency in how the app reads IMAP server responses that made downloading a big batch of messages slower than it needed to be, especially on the first sync of a large folder.
"All Inboxes" updates faster when one account syncs - it no longer re-merges and re-sorts every connected account's mail on each update, only the account that actually changed.

Fixed a bug where opening some messages showed nothing at all in the reading pane, with no error - a gap in how the app fell back to fetching a message's full content when its structure didn't declare a readable part up front.

Switching folders no longer shows a loading spinner over a message list that's already correctly loaded from cache. Background mail prefetching is also more considerate now, checking in with the app more often so it never keeps a folder switch or an opened message waiting as long as it used to.

Browsing a very large mailbox (tens of thousands of messages) no longer briefly freezes the window while the list re-sorts and re-groups - that work now happens in the background for big mailboxes, with typical mailboxes unaffected.

Moving a message no longer leaves its attachments and raw copy behind in the local cache forever - those are now cleaned up immediately, with a background sweep and periodic disk reclaim to catch anything left over from before this fix.

The dashboard no longer repaints on every sync event - it's debounced and skipped entirely while its tab isn't visible, though opening it or hitting Refresh still repaints right away. Folder switching, live search, and recipient/attendee autocomplete no longer briefly freeze the interface while reading from the local cache - those reads now happen in the background instead of blocking the window.

The message list no longer rebuilds every row when something changes - it now diffs the old and new content and updates only the rows that actually differ, instead of tearing down and rebuilding the whole visible list on every sync. Collapsed sections and conversations, and the current selection, are preserved exactly as before.

Draft autosave, folder-empty, and non-MOVE moves now expunge only the messages they just deleted, instead of the whole mailbox's deleted messages, on servers that support UIDPLUS. Moving, emptying, or archiving a sent message no longer re-lists the entire account to refresh folder counts - just the folders that actually changed. Fixed a bug where every sync double-counted each contact's address-book ranking. Fixed a UI-thread database write that could stall the app briefly when switching folders with snoozed messages present.

The IMAP connection is now DEFLATE-compressed (RFC 4978) on servers that advertise COMPRESS=DEFLATE, cutting 4-10x off the wire bytes for the first sync of a large folder, the background body prefetch, and the per-IDLE-wake flag fetch. The command is sent through a borrowing path, so a server that rejects it keeps the connection uncompressed instead of dropping it; Gmail, which doesn't advertise the capability, is untouched. async-imap is now vendored alongside imap-proto with the in-place stream-swap method this needs.

Inline cid: images that failed with "the server didn't return this attachment's part" now recover when the parts still exist. A part structure can go stale when a message is rewritten server-side after its body or summary was cached (mailing-list/gateway rewraps), so FetchAttachment now falls back to fetching the whole message and re-derives the part from the message's actual bytes - matched by Content-ID for inline images, else filename, else content type - and re-wrapped messages render their images and attachments again instead of broken placeholders. Parts genuinely gone still answer with the error toast, exactly as before.

The background body prefetch now downloads a whole batch of message bodies in one UID FETCH round trip instead of one per message - the query's part list is the union of the batch's text/calendar sections, each response is matched back to its message by UID, and the per-message cache checks and writes are batched too. A message the batch carries no text part for still degrades to the per-message whole-message fallback.

Folder counts now arrive with the folder list in one round trip on servers that support LIST-STATUS (RFC 5819): every folder's sidebar count - and its uidvalidity/uidnext, normally only learnable per-SELECT - is known the instant the list lands, instead of ~1 STATUS round trip per folder. Servers without the capability fall back to the plain LIST plus the STATUS drain exactly as before.

Every cache operation in the IMAP session now runs on tokio's blocking thread pool instead of the session's async worker, so a multi-second whole-folder write no longer stalls that account's actor (IDLE waits, command replies) or holds the shared worker against every other account's session. The one-time search-index backfill also no longer sits between startup and the first connection attempt - it now runs concurrently with the connect.

Every account/session event channel is now bounded (64 events) instead of unbounded, and each UI event loop drains its channel in batches, collapsing whole-snapshot events into the last copy of each - the startup burst no longer rebuilds the same surfaces once per queued copy, while non-snapshot events (new-mail notifications, body/part fetches, move/flag failures) are never dropped. The message list's "nothing changed" check is now allocation-free too.

Joined UID sets are now chunked into server-safe command lines: every UID FETCH/STORE/MOVE/COPY set is sorted, deduped, range-compressed (a dense folder's 100k UIDs collapse to one short 1:100000 command), and flushed before it exceeds a 40 KiB budget, so the first sync of a big folder can no longer tear the connection down with an over-long command line.

On CONDSTORE connections an IDLE wake no longer re-fetches the whole mailbox's flags: the steady-state sync issues a CHANGEDSINCE delta fetch - O(changed) instead of O(mailbox) - plus a UID SEARCH ALL to catch expunged messages. The envelope cache's per-sync write is now a diff instead of a whole-table rewrite: an upsert that rewrites nothing when nothing changed, deleting only expunged UIDs, so full-body search text survives later flag-only resyncs.

IMAP CONDSTORE is now enabled after login when the server advertises it, the first step of the incremental-sync roadmap: the per-mailbox highest-modseq baseline is captured from every SELECT (including the background prefetch, which selects most folders first) and from the STATUS count drain, survives re-lists, and is persisted in the cache - ready for CHANGEDSINCE delta fetches that will replace full-mailbox re-fetches on IDLE wakes. Servers without CONDSTORE are unaffected and keep syncing fully.

More of the optimisation roadmap: the SQLite cache layer's per-uid N+1s are gone. The background prefetch asks once which bodies are already cached instead of querying per UID; moving several messages deletes them all in one transaction; joined mark-read and tag-toggling batches patch every cached summary in one transaction with the same all-or-nothing contract as before; and snoozing a batch records all rows at once. Search results now load every hit's envelope in a single FTS-to-messages join instead of one query per hit, which matters on the UI thread where a keystroke can match hundreds of messages. A full audit of the rfc5464 path-name validator found its claimed quadratic rescan was already a linear single pass, so no change was needed there.

An optimisation pass over the IMAP pipeline, SQLite cache, and UI hot paths. IDLE wakes no longer re-SELECT the open folder or run a post-sync STATUS - the sync skips both when the session is already on that folder and derives the sidebar counts from the flags it just fetched. Server capabilities are read once after login instead of once per move batch. The mail cache runs with synchronous=NORMAL (the data is disposable and rebuilt from the server) and the calendar cache gains WAL plus a busy timeout. Search indexing skips the HTML strip for over-limit bodies, the reading pane's remote-content scan is cached per render, and the vendored imap-proto parser drops per-part-path Vec shifts, format!-and-to_string command-building temps, and complete-mode parsers that failed responses split across TCP segments - while a METADATA value with non-UTF-8 bytes now yields a parse error instead of a client crash.

Links in the email reading pane now open in the system's default browser instead of doing nothing - plain links and target="_blank" links alike (the latter were previously dropped as new-window requests), while the message body stays on screen. Only http/https go external; mailto: links remain blocked for now. Also silences the "Not loading module atk-bridge" console warning: GTK3-era accessibility modules are stripped from GTK_MODULES at startup, since GTK4 ships AT-SPI support natively.

Packaging fixes: the workspace Cargo.lock is now tracked in the repository (it was gitignored), so the Flatpak CI job can generate its offline cargo-sources.json on a fresh checkout and builds are reproducible; the Flatpak README is rewritten to match reality - the GOA settings deep-link works sandboxed over D-Bus, and cargo-sources.json is generated by CI.

The project is now formally licensed GPL-3.0-or-later: a canonical LICENSE file sits at the repository root and every Rust source file carries a copyright header naming Gavin Graham & Contributors. The README now leads with the Lookout logo and shows a message-reading screenshot below the feature list. Also fixes a build warning: the GResource bundle referenced two window-background files that no longer exist, so the stale entry was removed and the remaining one now names the real file - the bundle compiles cleanly again.

Config → Accounts gains a GNOME Online Accounts list with one on/off switch per discovered account, enabled by default. Flipping an account off stops Lookout from processing it entirely - its mail, calendars, reminders, tasks, and contacts disappear from every view and its sessions shut down; flipping it back on reconnects everything instantly. The choice persists across restarts, and a disabled account's local caches are kept so re-enabling needs no full resync.

Mail accounts no longer have to come from GNOME Online Accounts. Config → Accounts gains an "Add IMAP/SMTP account…" row for connecting a mail account by host, port, username, and password; these accounts sync, send, and appear in the sidebar exactly like GNOME Online Accounts ones, with their passwords kept in the GNOME keyring. Config → Mail accounts gains Edit and Remove actions for accounts added this way.

The Mail screen's calendar overview pane now lists your outstanding tasks below the selected day's events: every uncompleted task from every source (CalDAV, Google Tasks, local) in the dashboard's Overdue/Today/This week/Later order, in rows captioned to match the event list - a click opens the shared task editor. The list stays live as tasks are created, synced, completed, or removed.

The mail toolbar's flag-toggle button is renamed "Star/Unstar" and its icon now reflects the selected message's actual starred state - filled when starred, outline otherwise - instead of a single static icon.

The mail toolbar gains a "Follow-up" button that opens the task editor prefilled from the selected message (subject as title, sender and date noted for reference), defaulting to that email's own account's task list when it has one, or the local on-device list otherwise. Its icon fills in once a task has been created for the selected message.

The reading-pane header's "View contact" button now works: it looks the message's sender up across every connected contacts account - opening the contact editor for a found card, or a prefilled "New contact" form (sender name and email, address-book picker defaulting to the account the email lives in) when no address book has them.

Config → Appearance gains a "Dark message theme" switch: a default for newly-opened HTML messages (light mode - the original colours - by default), with the reading pane's per-message moon/sun toggle still overriding the current email either way.

The reading pane's "Switch message theme" toggle now reads its state: a moon icon that becomes a sun while the override is on, with tooltips naming what clicking will do next - "View in Dark Mode" off, "View in Light Mode" on.

The reading pane's "Switch message theme" toggle now works: for the email on screen it replaces the message's own background colour with the app theme's background, and inverts the text colours so the content still reads against it - a per-email override that resets when you move to the next message.
The Config sidebar now remembers its dragged width across resizes and restarts, the same way the Mail, Calendar, and Contacts panes already do.
The Config tab now uses a two-pane "tab groups" layout: a sidebar lists every settings section, and the right pane shows only the selected section's controls, instead of one long scrolling list.
Attachments in the Mail reading pane now open directly with their default app instead of showing a chooser dialog, double-clicking an attachment opens it, and attachment rows highlight on mouseover.

Marking a message read or unread from the Mail toolbar now updates instantly instead of waiting on the server; the button's icon is brighter and now shows a checkmark or an envelope depending on which action it will perform.

The mail-screen calendar overview pane's event list is easier to scan: each row now shows a calendar-colour dot, an aligned time (or "All Day") column, and the title, instead of a flat single-line row.

Dragging an event to a new time slot on the Calendar tab's Day/Week grid now moves it instantly and keeps it there while the change saves, instead of snapping back to the old slot until the server confirms.

Fixed the event editor's day-strip preview showing the event you're editing twice - once for the cached copy and again for the live preview of your unsaved edits. Editing now shows it once; other events on the same day, and creating a brand-new event, were never affected.

Deleting, archiving, or reporting a message as junk now removes it from the list the instant you click - it no longer waits several seconds for the server-side move to finish. If the move actually fails, the message reappears with an error toast instead of staying gone.
Added local .deb packaging support: ./build.sh --deb builds a release binary and packages it into a .deb using the existing cargo-deb metadata, without needing to push to CI.

Fixed dragging a message onto a folder in the folder pane not moving it. The drag started but the folder rows never accepted the drop: the internal payload was offered under a private mime type, and GTK only accepts a drop when the two sides' formats share a data type - so every drop was rejected before the move could run. The payload now travels as a standard bytes value, and the same fix covers dropping messages onto a tag row in the Categorize menu, which used the same mechanism. Dragging messages out of the app as .eml files still works as before.

Fixed invitations received from Outlook - a Teams meeting invite included - showing no way to respond. Outlook stamps its invites with Windows timezone IDs that the parser couldn't resolve, so the invitation banner never appeared; timezone resolution now falls back to a Windows-to-IANA mapping, so the invite parses with the correct DST-aware meeting time.

The Mail screen's mini-calendar overview pane now heads its day list with the selected date - "Today"/"Tomorrow" when relevant, otherwise the weekday + day + month (e.g. "Tue 12 Aug") - matching the Agenda view's day headers, so the list of events is always labeled with the day it's showing.

Fixed the mini-calendar overview pane getting clipped on the right edge when the main window is shrunk below the width needed to display it whole - the pane now auto-hides until a resize makes it fit again, and only comes back if the Calendar overview toggle is still enabled.

Fixed the folder pane collapsing a non-primary account's tree a few seconds after clicking into it - the tree is rebuilt on every folder update, and the rebuild now preserves each account group's collapse state, the selected folder, and the scroll position, while an account that is still connecting stays expandable instead of rendering as a permanently-collapsed row.

Fixed the Sent folder sometimes showing an unread-count badge for a message that had just been sent, or for mail that landed there from another device or client - any mailbox recognized as Sent now has the read flag enforced centrally as new messages arrive, so it never carries an unread badge regardless of what put the mail there.

Fixed switching folders leaving the previous folder's messages on screen until the new folder's own data arrived - the message list now repaints from the newly-selected folder's own cache immediately, and shows a "Fetching message list." spinner while a folder that isn't cached yet loads.

Fixed sent messages not appearing in the Sent folder, and new mail sometimes not appearing in a folder's message list even though the sidebar already showed an updated unread count - including when the folder was the one already open.

Fixed inserting and sending inline images in the composer: the "Insert image" button did nothing when clicked before the message body had been focused, a body that was only an image with no other text silently sent as blank, and - the main event - a security setting meant to protect the inline-image mechanism was inadvertently blocking the reading pane's own page from displaying it, so a correctly-sent inline image never actually appeared when viewing the message. Also fixed folder refresh being slow and new mail sometimes not appearing until restart, and an interaction (opening a message, switching folders) landing during a connection retry being silently dropped instead of answered once reconnected.

Fixed sending to a contact picked from the address book sometimes failing with "Invalid recipient Address" - a recipient with a display name attached to it was being rejected by the SMTP send instead of being sent correctly.
Trash and Junk folders now have an expunge quick action: hovering a folder row shows an "Empty" button that permanently deletes all messages in that folder after a confirmation.

The composer now supports full HTML emails: attach files (shown as removable chips), insert or paste images directly into the body as inline pictures, and format with text alignment, font family, horizontal rules, indent/outdent, remove-formatting, and table insertion alongside the existing bold/italic/lists/color/link tools.

Reworked the composer's header: Cc/Bcc are now reveal buttons on the To row, "Request read receipt" is a toggle icon next to the pop-out button, Cancel is a red trash icon, and the From selector moved into the header next to Send. Fixed the popped-out compose window's controls staying invisible after popping back in, and a leftover highlighted card sometimes left over the background after cancelling a message.
Fixed the Config (settings) icon at the bottom of the left nav rail occasionally going invisible about a second after startup, staying that way until the window was manually resized.

Read receipts (RFC 8098). The composer gains a "Request read receipt" switch that adds a Disposition-Notification-To header, so recipients can notify you when they read your message. On the receiving side, a message that asks for a receipt shows a "Send read receipt" banner in the reading pane - or, under the new Config → Mail "Send read receipts automatically" setting, the receipt is sent silently the moment the message is displayed. The receipt is a proper multipart/report document (a human-readable part, the disposition fields with the message's original Message-ID, and the original message's headers), is marked as auto-generated so automated senders don't loop, and is sent once per message per session - never for machine-generated mail or for other reports.

A new Birthdays calendar, synthesized from your contacts: every contact with a birthday appears as an all-day event in a "Birthdays" row of the calendar sidebar, with its own colour and show/hide toggle. Dated birthdays show the age ("Alice's 36th birthday"); yearless ones (the --MMDD form or Apple's X-APPLE-OMIT-YEAR) recur every year; and Feb 29 lands on Feb 28 in non-leap years. Birthdays appear in every calendar surface - month, week and day grids, the agenda, print, the mini-calendar's event-day markers, the Mail overview and the dashboard - update live whenever your contacts resync, and fire a notification when the day begins. The events are read-only, with the editor explaining that they're synthesized from contacts rather than savable. vCard BDAY parsing now also accepts the yearless forms, and reminder notifications for all-day events say "All day" instead of "Starts at 00:00".

The Config → Keyboard shortcuts list no longer fills the page: the nineteen binding rows and "Restore default shortcuts" now live inside a collapsible "Keyboard shortcuts" row that starts folded, so the section reads as a single line until you expand it to see or edit a binding.

Global keyboard shortcuts, matched by physical key so they work no matter what keyboard layout you use: New message (Ctrl+N), Reply (Ctrl+R), Reply all, Forward, Delete, Archive, Report junk, Snooze, Flag, Mark read/unread, Print, Find (Ctrl+F), closing the reading pane (Esc), and Ctrl+1-6 to jump between Mail, Calendar, People, Tasks, Lookout and Settings.

Config → General now lists every shortcut, and clicking one records a new key combination: plain Escape cancels, modifier-free typing keys and dead keys are refused, and a chord already used by another action is rejected with a toast. "Restore default shortcuts" puts everything back, and your bindings are remembered between sessions.

Lookout's look is now fully themeable. Every colour the app drew is a named token that follows the system light/dark scheme where that makes sense (unread accents, muted text, chips), while the deliberately fixed surfaces (the translucent panes over the background artwork, the toolbar bands, the amber flag) stay put. Config → Appearance gains a Theme dropdown - System, Flat Dark (the classic look), or Flat Light - plus a Custom accent color switch and picker that recolour buttons and selections app-wide, both persisting between sessions and applying live.
Fixed: picking a custom accent colour no longer trips a GTK assertion - the picker's dialog is now created explicitly, so the colour dialog opens and applies normally.

Print support lands everywhere: the reading pane's More menu prints the message you're reading (HTML bodies print from the reading pane's own view, plain-text bodies via a wrapped page), the event editor's Print button prints the event details, and the Calendar toolbar prints the month you're viewing as an agenda.

Recurring events can finally be edited per occurrence: the event editor now offers This occurrence / This and following / All events scopes, recurring events can be drag-rescheduled (each drag moves just that instance), and deleting one instance of a series removes exactly that instance instead of the whole event - all through proper RECURRENCE-ID and EXDATE overrides that sync back to your calendar.

Mail gains drag and drop: drag messages onto any folder to move them, onto a tag in the Categorize menu to tag them, or out of the app to save them as .eml files - dragging a multi-selection carries the whole batch.

Calendar event chips can now be dragged to a new time: in the Day/Week/Work week grids a chip press becomes a drag once the pointer moves (moving the whole event, or grabbing its bottom edge to resize the end, snapped to half hours and clamped to the visible week, with a translucent ghost following the pointer), and in the Month/Split views a chip drags across day cells, live re-parented with the target cell highlighted. Drops persist through the editor's own etag-guarded update path; recurring events and webcal subscription events are read-only to drag for now.

All the pop-out / pop-back-in buttons now use matching bundled icons: a pop-out glyph on the compose header and the People toolbar's "Open in new window" (now icon-only with a tooltip), and a pop-in glyph on the "Back to main window" buttons in both popped-out windows.

Message list rows now carry small attachment and meeting-invite icons right after the sender name: a paperclip when the message has attachments and a calendar glyph when it carries an iCalendar part (a thread header shows each if any of its messages has one). Both are dimmed below the subject text and the flag, with tooltips, and hidden entirely on plain rows.

The composer can be popped out into its own window: a button in the compose header moves it to a standalone window (with its own title bar holding Cancel, Send, and a Back button), where draft autosave keeps running. Closing the window - or using Back - pops the composer back into the reading pane with everything intact.

Fixed a spate of GTK "Failed to set text … from markup" warnings: Adw rows (like Config's "Sending identities" subtitle) parse their titles as Pango markup by default, so identity labels such as "Name <address>" - and the remaining dynamic error toasts that weren't escaped yet - are now escaped so <, >, &, and friends display literally.

Conversations in the message list: replies are now grouped under collapsible thread headers (a sender/subject/date line with a participant-count badge) under the default By Date sort, with each conversation placed by its newest message and its messages shown oldest-first. A new Conversations toggle in the View tab turns the grouping off and on, and the setting persists between sessions. Thread headers aren't selection targets - batch actions, quick actions, and the reading pane still work on individual messages.

Composing is cleaner: the composer's "Manage identities…" row and "Rich text" switch are now handled in Config - Manage identities lives under each account in Config → Mail accounts, and the Rich text setting in Config → Mail picks the editor your new messages open in, with the mid-compose plain/rich toggle still available in the editor's formatting toolbar. Also fixed: the nav rail's Config button no longer disappears when the window is made very short - the rail scrolls instead of clipping it.

New: the Lookout dashboard tab. A new header-corner tab (with the app's Observatorium telescope icon) shows your connected accounts at a glance - people most contacted, emails by time of day, outstanding tasks, and upcoming calendar events - fed from the local caches and the calendar sessions, live-updating as mail, events, and tasks change. Upcoming events now span the current and next month and stay populated while the dashboard is on screen. The search entry moves beside the tab in the header.

Saving drafts works again: draft autosaves and the copy of a sent message kept in Sent were being rejected by the server as malformed, so a draft never appeared in your Drafts folder. Error messages shown as toasts (account failures, contacts import/export problems, and more) also display properly now instead of tripping a GTK markup warning when they contain addresses or angle brackets.
The Calendar and People sidebars now remember their widths between sessions: drag them to size and the split comes back exactly as you left it, on restart and when the window is resized.

Emails with calendar invitations now show the event's details: a card above the message body displays when the event is (local time, or the date for all-day events, with a recurring hint), where it is, who organized it, and any description - alongside the usual accept/deny bar.

The People tab's left pane now matches the calendar and mail panes: its category list is transparent, so the window background image shows through the translucent card the same way the other modules' sidebars do.

Tasks get real sources: Google Tasks now connects through the Tasks API (its CalDAV is events-only) with its own sign-in, task lists appearing alongside calendar tasks; when no service can hold tasks, new ones are saved locally on this device instead of being refused. The Tasks screen explains which situation you're in, and the Google Tasks OAuth client id can be set in Config instead of an environment variable.

Tasks arrive: a new Tasks tab backed by CalDAV to-do items (VTODO) shows your tasks grouped by Overdue / Today / This week / Later / Completed, with one-click completion and a full editor for summary, notes, due date, priority, and progress. Tasks sync from every connected calendar account on a schedule and are cached locally for instant startup paint.

People gets an offline-friendly overhaul: contacts are cached locally per account (the People tab paints instantly at startup and the Deleted list survives restarts), and contact sync now uses incremental server deltas instead of full refetches. The whole People screen can be popped out into its own window with a Back to main window button, and contact autocomplete in the composer and event invites now runs through one shared CardDAV-backed provider.

Contacts become fully editable: create, edit, and delete contacts from the People tab, with changes written back to your CardDAV address books. The new Manage groups dialog renames or removes contact groups (your vCard categories) across every account, and contacts can be imported from or exported to .vcf files - importing updates existing contacts by their UID and skips duplicates by email.

Nextcloud (and any CalDAV/CardDAV account whose login differs from its display name) can now connect: DAV requests authenticate with the account's login instead of its display name, GOA's stored URLs are cleaned up (embedded usernames stripped, missing trailing slash restored), and server error pages are sanitized before they reach toasts and status labels.

Calendar feeds and file import: the Add calendar button now opens a dialog to subscribe to a webcal feed - events appear read-only, refreshing automatically - to import an .ics file into one of your calendars (re-importing updates, not duplicates), or to manage existing subscriptions.

Calendar events can now remind you: when an event with a reminder comes due, a notification appears with Open, Snooze 5 minutes, and Dismiss actions - opening the event straight in the editor. Reminders that came due while the app was closed appear on launch (until the event starts), each alert fires only once, and a new Config → Calendar → Event alerts switch controls them all.

Accounts can now send as multiple identities: the composer has a From selector, identities carry a display name (which now actually appears in the From header), Reply-To and blind-copy addresses, and a Manage identities dialog - reachable from the composer and from Config - stores them per account.

The reading pane now recognizes iMIP invitations: a banner appears for calendar emails, letting you accept, tentatively accept, or decline - sending an RFC 6047 reply back to the organizer and saving the event into your calendar - or remove a cancelled event.

The Calendar's main grid is now clickable: click a day or an empty time slot to highlight it, and click it again to open the New Event editor prefilled for that moment - a month grid day opens one for 9am, a Day or Week grid slot for the exact time you clicked. You can also click and drag across the Day or Week grid to highlight a whole range of time, and clicking the range opens the editor spanning exactly what you selected.

The New Event dialog's attendee field now offers autocomplete from your mail history and address books. The header bar's search field also picked up a darker background so it stands out from the surrounding bar.

The Calendar's New Event dialog is rebuilt with a fuller feature set: invite attendees, set up a recurring series, add a video call link, and set categories, sensitivity, and a reminder - all from a new toolbar, alongside a live mini-calendar and day preview showing where the event lands.

Messages can be exported as .eml files - a new "More" menu on the ribbon fetches the whole raw message on demand and caches it locally, so re-exports are instant and offline. The reading pane also shows a List-Unsubscribe banner when a mailing list advertises one, with one-click unsubscribing (RFC 8058) and a mailto fallback that opens the composer pre-filled.

The bundled artwork - the window background, the Mail/Calendar/People rail icons, and the app icon itself - now ships inside the binary as a compiled GResource bundle, so every build renders identically whether or not the icon is installed system-wide. Builds without the resource compiler fall back to the old embedded copies automatically.

Lookout now builds its own distribution packages - .deb, .rpm, Flatpak, and snap - through a CI workflow, so it can be installed as a regular package on any Linux desktop. The Open Online Accounts Settings button also works inside those sandboxes, opening the settings panel over D-Bus instead of launching a system program.

Search moves into the window's title bar: a permanent search field is always visible, and pressing Ctrl+F jumps straight to it with the previous query selected. Searching from any tab - Mail, Calendar, or People - now switches to Mail so the results are on screen.

The folder and message list panes now remember how wide you made them, and keep their proportions when the window is resized. The folder pane is bounded on both sides: it can't shrink below 200px or grow past 320px.

Each attachment's action is now a menu: open it with the default application for its type, pick another app with "Open With" (via the desktop portal's chooser), or save it to disk - opening uses a temporary copy that's cleaned up when Lookout closes.

Attachments can now be saved - each one gets a row under the message with a Save button that fetches its bytes on demand, caches them on disk, and offers a save dialog. Saving that worked before sometimes never finished; that's fixed, along with the fallback path that misnumbered parts.
Your preferences now stick around between sessions - pane layout, sort order, favorites, and the Mail and Appearance settings are remembered. Starred contacts are saved too.

The calendar is now editable - a new Event button and clicking any event open an editor to create, change, or delete events, written back to your CalDAV account. Recurring events can be edited as a whole series.

Full-text search is here - press Ctrl+F (or the toolbar's Search button) to search across every synced folder and account, with results shown instantly from a local SQLite FTS5 index and a live IMAP search filling in the gaps. Clicking any result opens the message no matter which folder it lives in.

Folders now show all their mail instead of just the most recent few hundred - the Gmail inboxes that were missing older messages and large folders like All Mail are fixed. The message list also groups mail older than a year under year headings, so old mail is easier to find than one long "Older" section.

You can now select multiple messages at once - ctrl/shift-click, or toggle Select mode next to the favourite star to swap each row's avatar for a checkbox. With messages selected, Delete, Archive, Report, Flag/Unflag, Snooze, and a new Mark read/unread button all act on the whole selection at once, and the reading pane shows how many messages are selected.

Messages can now be color-tagged. A Categorize button in the toolbar (and a right-click menu on a message) assigns one of your tags to the selected message, which stores a keyword on it so the tag follows it across devices. Tagged messages show small color dots in the list. A Manage tags dialog lets you create, rename, recolour, or remove tags. Deleting, archiving, or reporting a message now also removes it from the list the moment the move succeeds, instead of waiting a few seconds for a full mailbox resync to finish.

The People tab's left side now shows Your Contacts, Favourites, Your contact lists, and Deleted for each account, plus a Categories section for any tags you use. You can star a contact as a favourite from the contact list. This release also fixes several bugs that could leave an account's contacts showing empty, including one that silently dropped every contact from any address book using the very common older vCard format.

Lookout now includes a Contacts tab with a split layout: categories on the left and a filtered contact list on the right. Opening a contact shows a details dialog with richer information from synced address books.

Composer recipient suggestions now include contacts from your online address books, not just recent correspondents from mail history, and contact sync refreshes in the background. This release also improves Contacts groundwork with GNOME Online Accounts contacts discovery and CardDAV integration.
The message list starts wider, the space between it and the reading pane is narrower, and the folder pane can no longer be dragged narrower than its folder names.

Events that last more than one day now show on every day they run in the Calendar month view, instead of just their first day - including events that started before the month you are viewing. The mini calendar's event-day markers and the Mail screen's day list count every covered day too.

Recipients in the composer are now individual chips you can remove one at a time, instead of a line of comma-separated text, and typing suggests people you have exchanged mail with. A Bcc field joins To and Cc.
Fixes a crash that closed the application a few seconds after opening the composer, and stops draft autosave from leaving duplicate drafts behind.
Opening a message now marks it as read, and the toolbar's Flag button marks a message for follow-up. Flagged messages show a marker in the message list.
Fixes for the window background picker added in the previous release.
You can now choose your own image for the window background, in Settings under Appearance, and restore the bundled artwork at any time. Your choice is remembered between sessions.

Microsoft 365 accounts added in GNOME Online Accounts now work: they appear in the account list and sign in correctly. Repeated connection-failure notifications no longer pile up while the application is reconnecting.

The composer can now write formatted mail - bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, bulleted and numbered lists, font sizes, text colour, and links - and sends a plain-text copy alongside it for recipients whose mail client cannot show formatting. Formatting can be turned off by default in Settings under Mail.

The message list gained column headings for Sender, Subject, and Date. A new Settings option under Mail controls whether images hosted on remote servers are loaded when reading a message; it is off by default.
Fixes a folder that could stay empty after clicking it quickly, and new mail not appearing in the folder you were reading. Background downloading of message bodies no longer delays your own clicks.
Switching folders feels roughly twice as fast: the previously seen messages appear immediately while the server is still responding.
Folders you have opened before now show their messages instantly, from a local copy, rather than waiting for the server.
Messages you have already opened now display instantly instead of being downloaded again, and a message whose images are hosted on a slow or unreachable server no longer holds up the reading pane.
The calendar overview pane on the right of the Mail screen is now about half as wide, leaving more room for the message list and reading pane.

The message list has a new look: each message shows a sender avatar, the subject, the date, and a preview of the message body. Unread messages are highlighted, and messages are now grouped under collapsible date headings such as Today, Yesterday, and Older.

The message list has a new header: it names the folder you are reading and the account it belongs to, and adds controls to sort the list by date, sender, or subject, sync the open folder, and star a folder into a Favorites section at the top of the folder tree.
Initial release: browse folders, read mail, and send plain-text messages through an account configured in GNOME Online Accounts.
